chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Maruk ibn Ubayd, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'What do these people say regarding the man who misses two rak'at with the Imam?' I said: 'They say he should recite Al-Hamd and a Surah in them.' He said: 'This is one who overturns his prayer, making its beginning its end.' I said: 'How should he deal with it?' He said: 'He should recite the Opening of the Book in every rak'ah.'
ai.seo_question: How should a person who joins the Imam late and misses two rak'at perform their prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) refutes the opinion that a latecomer should recite a full Surah for missed rak'at, arguing that this approach inverts the prayer's structure by treating the missed portion as a complete, independent unit. Instead, he prescribes reciting only Al-Fatihah in each rak'ah, a ruling that aligns with the principle of *qasr* (shortening) and ensures the latecomer's prayer remains an extension of the Imam's rather than a separate, duplicated entity. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the structural integrity of congregational prayer and the specific legal status of the *ma'mum* joining late.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Marouk Bin Ubeyd, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Which thing are they (people) saying regarding the man who misses out on two Rak’at with the Imam?’ I said, ‘They are saying he should recite in these two with Al-Hamd (Chapter 1) and a (another) Chapter’. So heasws said: ‘This is one who overturns his Salāt, making its beginning to be its end’. I said, ‘How should he deal with it?’ Heasws said: ‘He should recite the Opening of the Book (Chapter 1) during each Rak’at’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Marwak ibn ’Ubayd from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from a man who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once asked, ‘What do they say about a man who has missed two Rak‘at of the Imam’s Salah (prayer)?’

I replied, ‘They say that he is to recite al-Hamd and Surah (chapter) in them.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He turns his Salah (prayer) backward by making its first the last.’ I then asked, ‘How is he to do it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He recites al-Fatihah al-Kitab in every Rak‘at.’”
